verses.text: The LORD said to Moses,
"Command the people of Israel to bring you pure oil from pressed olives for the lamps, so that they can be kept burning all the time.

In the Tent of Meeting, outside the curtain in front of the Covenant Box, Aaron must keep the lamps burning before the LORD from evening until morning, always. This is a rule forever for all your families to come.
He must always look after the lamps on the pure gold lampstand before the LORD.
Take fine flour and bake twelve loaves, using about three kilograms of flour for each loaf.
Put them in two rows, six in each row, on the pure gold table before the LORD.
Put pure incense along each row. It will be the part that is remembered for the bread, a gift made by fire to the LORD.
Every Sabbath day the bread must be set out before the LORD, always. It is a covenant forever for the people of Israel.
The bread belongs to Aaron and his sons, and they must eat it in a holy place. It is a most holy part of the gifts made by fire to the LORD, their share forever."
There was a man whose mother was an Israelite and whose father was an Egyptian. He went out among the people of Israel, and a fight broke out in the camp between him and an Israelite man.
The son of the Israelite woman spoke against the holy Name of the LORD and cursed. So they brought him to Moses. His mother's name was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, from the tribe of Dan.
They kept him under guard until the LORD would make clear to them what to do.
Then the LORD said to Moses,
"Take the man who cursed outside the camp. All who heard him must put their hands on his head, and then the whole community must stone him.
Tell the people of Israel: Anyone who curses his God will carry the blame for his sin.

Anyone who speaks against the name of the LORD must be put to death. The whole community must stone him. Whether he is a foreigner or born in the land, if he speaks against the Name, he must be put to death.
Anyone who kills another person must be put to death.
Anyone who kills someone's animal must replace it, a life for a life.
If anyone injures his neighbour, the same must be done to him as he has done:
a broken bone for a broken bone, an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth. Whatever injury he has caused must be done to him.
Whoever kills an animal must replace it, but whoever kills a person must be put to death.
You must have the same law for the foreigner and for the one born in the land. I am the LORD your God."
Moses told this to the people of Israel. They took the man who had cursed outside the camp and stoned him to death. The people of Israel did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
